decisions.summary: A new text check, l7r-gate check guard-deps, run by make static after the conflict check, refusing a manifest that names l7r_guard and naming l7r_shared with its path and rust/guard/shared for guard-only pieces.

decisions.summary: Walk every Cargo.toml under rust/ on disk (target and hidden directories and symlinks not walked), not git-listed, because the workspace's gate/crates/* glob builds untracked crates too.
decisions.why: The filed scope is manifests under rust/, which holds the workspace whose rebuild count T58 measured. Walking the disk rather than git's list widens the reach to untracked crates the glob builds, so nothing is narrowed. Item 4 records a grep showing no manifest under tests/ or scripts/ names the guard.

decisions.summary: Only the guard's own manifest is exempt.
decisions.why: The task line exempts the binaries that ship the guard. Item 4 records that l7r-guard.sh and hookbench build it with -p l7r_guard and no dependency, and cargo tree -i shows no dependent, so the guard's own manifest is the whole of that exemption. The exemption is exactly as large as the filed one, no larger.

decisions.summary: Forms read: a key in any dependency table (normal, dev, build, target, workspace; - and _ alike; dotted or quoted keys), a [*dependencies.l7r_guard] table, a rename through package, and comments cut at #. A path-only dependency under another key is not read, because cargo refuses one (measured probe); the check looks at direct dependencies only.
decisions.why: The forms come from Cargo's manifest format. The one form left out cannot build: the probe records cargo refusing it ('no matching package named hooks'), so leaving it out is not a carve-out. Any transitive dependency needs some manifest under rust/ to name the guard directly, and the check refuses that manifest, so checking direct dependencies alone loses nothing of the purpose.

decisions.summary: Record each run as check-guard-deps and add its entry to scripts/tool-registry.json, because check tool-signals went red without it.
decisions.why: This is the project's existing rule for a recorded tool, and the entry is needed for the requested check to pass hooks-test. It enforces the request and adds no behavior.

decisions.id: T67-(b)3 a checkout of this project outside the mirror and the clones
decisions.summary: in_tree now counts a COPY of this project anywhere as the tree, known by what the directory is: its common git dir is the mirror's or a clone's, or its origin is this repository (by path, file://, or the mirror's own origin by any scheme). Measured: 17 of 1,289 git work trees under /tmp are copies, and the suite's section 6 and two crate tests pin it. The work-tree-making breadth and the hop bound are judged as their own decisions below.
decisions.why: Round 1's NOT LEGITIMATE is resolved for a copy that is on disk. A README written in a builder's /tmp worktree or clone of this project is now refused, so constitution XVII's purpose holds for the agents most likely to break it. I re-read /tmp/t67/copies-guard2.txt (1,290 lines). It has 17 COPY lines, matching the block's list: 2 worktrees whose common git dir is the clone's, 13 clones by path, a file:// clone and a clone of that. It also has 138 passing lines whose printed origin is this repository, and all 138 have an empty common dir. Those are the unreadable stubs the block's item 7 explains: /tmp/t04/replay/clone and /tmp/t07-replay.ZmMH/c, the two that are not l7r- fixtures, each have an empty .git directory. So no repository git reads as this project's passes. The green logs are present (suite 75 passed, 0 failed; crate 421 passed).

decisions.id: T67-(b)3a classify left unchanged; the wider check lives in readme_hooks' own in_tree
decisions.summary: The brief said 'fix classify'. Instead shared::tree::classify stays as it is, and the README guard asks whether a path is a copy of this project in its own in_tree.
decisions.why: This deviation from the brief changes HOW the result is reached, not what was asked, so it carries no ruling. The brief is the session's words, not the GM's, and neither the request nor the accepted spec says where the check lives. The outcome round 1 required, a README in a copy of this project refused, holds and is pinned. Widening classify would have changed Target.class for every walk, so main_tree_hooks would move /tmp-copy writes that it calls the mirror's for no reason. That would be a wrong outcome in another guard, and keeping classify narrow avoids it.

decisions.summary: The 2026-10-10 command (rm -rf $d, mkdir, cd $d, git init, printf x > README, no remote added) is classified as not a copy of this project, so it passes under (b)1, its whole command pinned in section 6.

It has no remote, clone, fetch, worktree or origin, and its write targets are README and specs/399-live-test/spec.md in a directory it makes afresh and runs git init in. So it has its own common git dir and no origin, it is not this project's, and it passes under (b)1.

decisions.id: T67-(b)3c a command that makes a work tree of this project: every README it writes counts as the tree's
decisions.summary: makes_ours: when a Bash command itself runs git worktree add of the tree or git clone of this repository, every README-named target that command writes is refused, wherever it lies. The block chose this breadth 'over reading which path lies in the new tree', and its own example is refused: `git worktree add /tmp/t58/wt && cp rust/guard/src/guards/readme_hooks.rs /tmp/t58/readme.keep`.
decisions.why: This refuses T67's own case, a README-named scratch file outside the tree, whenever the same command also makes a work tree. Builders open their work that way (git worktree add /tmp/tNN/wt && ...). It is excepted from the block's goal A.1 (never refused for 'a /tmp scratch file') and from the brief's 'a path outside the tree passing', and the block's item 12 and 'Found and left? none' both say otherwise. The ground given is a choice, not impossibility: the walk already resolves where the new work tree goes, since it writes its probe touch there, so whether a target lies under that place is a path comparison on what the guard already holds. Nothing in the request implies it, and following the rule literally would not defeat its purpose, because a README under the new tree would still be refused. 'The old guard refused it too' and '0 corpus hits' did not save L1 in round 1 and do not save this. A check that refuses good work is a defect (XIV, 449 T196). Required, either of two: (a) judge whether each README-named target lies under the new work tree's resolved place, refusing one inside it and passing one outside it, failing closed where the place is unresolved, and pin in the suite and the crate, red first, that `git worktree add /tmp/t58/wt && cp rust/guard/src/guards/readme_hooks.rs /tmp/t58/readme.keep` passes while `git worktree add /tmp/t58/wt && echo x > /tmp/t58/wt/README.md` (and a cd-into-it relative write) is refused; or (b) record it under Found and left with its why, a filed task id and 'lands before ...' as FR-009 requires, and correct item 12.

decisions.id: T67-(b)3d origin chains followed three hops
decisions.summary: A local repository whose origin is itself a copy is followed at most three hops; a copy of this project four or more clones removed from the mirror or a clone passes.
decisions.why: This hook runs on every Bash call that names a README, and item 8's budget gives its disk reads a fixed bound: at most one .git, one commondir and two config files a hop, with no process started. Following origins needs some limit, because local origins can chain without end. The measured world is well inside this one: the census's deepest copy is one hop (/tmp/t40/sh2, a clone of the file:// clone /tmp/t40/sh1), and no chain of two or more exists among 1,289 work trees. So the bound removes no protection the guard actually gives, and the rule's purpose, refusing a README in a builder's worktree or clone, holds in full. This is a stated, measured bound, not a case carved out against the rule.

decisions.id: T67-L1 a README write held as a one-line string's text

Since the known defect is fixed, 'Found and left? none' is now accurate. The blanking only drops strings that themselves hold a quoted string, so a plain open('docs/README.md', 'w') still resolves and is refused.

decisions.id: D1 the cap reads the builder's own last message iteration
decisions.summary: usage_of reads input, cache read and cache creation from the last usage.iterations entry of type message, and context() (the cap's reader) goes through it, instead of the top-level sum that adds both of the builder's own iterations around an advisor call
decisions.why: FR-006 refuses a builder's call once ITS context is past the threshold. Item 4 measured that on every one of the 581 advisor rows the top level is the sum of the builder's two own iterations (about twice its context), that the advisor's iteration is a separate model's, and that the builder's next call read 152,979 after a 300,884 top level. Reading the doubled sum refused 33 builders at 151k to 290k, well under the 300k knob: that is a wrong outcome against FR-006 and request improvement 1 (keep builder contexts small, not stop them at half), so fixing the reader makes the requirement do what it says. No exception is made.

decisions.summary: the top level is read only where the row has no iterations list, no message entry, or an own iteration of zero
decisions.why: Item 4 measured 6 rows with no list. On those, and on the single-iteration rows (27,506), the top level is the builder's own context, so the fallback keeps the existing correct reading where there is nothing else to read. It narrows nothing FR-006 asks.

decisions.summary: the 300k constant stays; only how it is read changes
decisions.why: FR-006 sets the knob at 300k (GUESS, tuned from FR-004's data) and nothing in the request or spec asks to move it with this fix. Leaving it means a builder now meets the cap FR-006 actually states.

decisions.id: D4 the event log's ctx fixed by the same change
decisions.summary: ctx calls context(), so it now records the builder's own context on an advisor row rather than the doubled sum
decisions.why: ctx is the per-call context figure FR-004/FR-005's readers and FR-006's tuning depend on ('the knob tuned from FR-004's data'). The same doubled read was a wrong figure; fixing it with the one shared reader serves the request's measurement half.

decisions.id: D5 tok keeps the billed top level
decisions.summary: call_of, the event log's cost figure, keeps the top-level sum, because both of the builder's own iterations are billed; the parse is shared through message_of
decisions.why: FR-004 asks for an agent's token cost. Both own iterations are billed calls, so their sum is the builder's own cost. Leaving tok on the top level keeps that correct, rather than carrying the context fix into a figure where it would be wrong.

decisions.id: D6 the advisor's own tokens left out of tok, deferred to T69
